description.narrative:
The proposed project is part of a comprehensive ADB package which also includes budget support for the COVID-19 Active Response and Expenditure Support (CARES) Program. The proposed project will be co-financed by ADB and AIIB to urgently increase Uzbekistan's resilience to COVID-19 pandemics and other epidemics. The project will support the testing, surveillance, and case management of COVID-19 in Uzbekistan by equipping and refurbishing the national laboratory system, establishing an IT-based national surveillance and monitoring system, and improving and expanding the COVID-19 treatment capacity. Activities will be coordinated with, and complementary to, assistance of the World Bank, the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), and fill remaining gaps in medical equipment and supplies.
The proposed project is aligned with four operational priorities of Strategy 2030: (i) addressing poverty and reducing inequalities through improved health access; (ii) accelerating gender equality through occupational safety and training targets for women; (iii) strengthening governance and institutional capacity; and (iv) fostering regional cooperation through reducing risks of cross-border disease transmission. The project further aligns with Uzbekistan's National Actions Strategy for 2017-2021, and the government-adopted "The Concept of Development of the Healthcare System of the Republic of Uzbekistan for 2019-2025." Reforms will address systematic health systems issues such as fragmentation, inefficiency, and the insufficient emphasis on non-communicable diseases prevention and early detection.
The project is aligned with (i) concept for the development of the health system of the Republic of Uzbekistan for 2019-2025, and (ii) the SPRP. The project will have the following outcome: resilience to outbreaks of COVID-19 and other epidemics reinforced. The project will have three outputs: Output 1 - national laboratory system strengthened; Output 2 - national surveillance and response system established for COVID-19 and other epidemics; and Output 3 - COVID-19 treatment capacity expanded.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: COVID-19 and other infectious diseases treatment and diagnostic capacity expanded Indicator: All 14 project-supported infectious disease hospitals upgraded with diagnostic and treatment equipment (2020 baseline: 0) Achievement: 16 Progress/Status: 14 hospitals now equipped. Data Source: MOH compliance checks, midterm review special audit, and post-project special audit reports

Output: COVID-19 and other infectious diseases treatment and diagnostic capacity expanded Indicator: All frontline staff (at least 80% of whom are women) in 16 project hospitals have improved skills in infection prevention control and gender-sensitive patient management to treat COVID-19 cases and other infectious respiratory diseases (baseline: 0%) Achievement: 40 Progress/Status: Training on medical staff new equipment at upgraded laboratories. Training coverage: • Training of medical and technical staff of project institutions in the use of supplied medical and non-medical equipment • Training of medical and technical staff of project facilities on "health, safety and environment" according to ADB/AIIB/UNOPS standards and guidelines (Sept 2024) • Training on the implementation of information and communication technologies (Sept 2024) • Training on infection prevention and infection control for medical staff (including laboratory technicians) of project facilities • Staff training on prevention of the spread of highly dangerous infections, safety measures and quality of medical care, as well as on "pandemic preparedness and response" (July 2024)
Data Source: Training firm report, midterm review special audit, post-project special audit reports, and project monitoring system

Output: COVID-19 and other infectious diseases treatment and diagnostic capacity expanded Indicator: Ambulance services are expanded with 1,000 ambulances providing a nationwide coverage (2020 baseline: 0) Achievement: 780 Progress/Status: 1,000 ambulances delivered. Final payments under ADB and AIIB loans disbursed. Data Source: MOH reports

Output: National laboratory system strengthened Indicator: At least 30 project-supported laboratories compliant with Biosafety Level 2 requirements and Good Laboratory Practice or equivalent standards, including sex-segregated sanitation facilities (2020 baseline: 0) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Infrastructure, equipment, training, and IT support to labs underway to support BSL compliance. As of June 2025, overall project implementation against planned updated schedule and scope delivery is assessed at 45%. Civil works (41%), equipment for SES centers (36%), ICT (75%), training (54%). Procurement of 1000 ambulances and equipment for 14 hospitals have been completed. Construction works have been mobilized at 11 sites. Equipment for first batches of equipment for SES labs ($8 million worth) have been completed and under delivery. Assessment of BSL compliance following completion of laboratory upgrades will follow.
As of Sep 2025: (contracts awarded)for 154 items of medical and non-medical equipment.. Five types of ICT equipment under NFS successfully delivered to designated users.
As of Jan 2026: civil works contracts across 45 project sites: 33 contracts have been awarded, with 4 more to be awarded by end January, while 12 remaining contracts will by 1st week of February. Total number of civil works packages was 46 initially, but 1 was canceled, leaving 45 active sites. Data Source: MOH compliance checks based on WHO guidelines, midterm review special audit, and post-project special audit reports

Output: National laboratory system strengthened Indicator: At least 500,000 additional regular PCR tests to detect COVID-19 conducted by January 2025, prioritizing frontline health workers (80% of whom are women) and pregnant patients (10 June 2020 baseline: 830,000) Achievement: 3628800 Progress/Status: Achieved. Between baseline (mid-2020) and pandemic's end (mid-2023): nearly 30 million PCR tests were conducted. National protocols were updated at least 7 times during the pandemic, and these protocols also included aspects prioritizing health workers and pregnant women.
Data Source: Laboratory records and MOH

Output: National surveillance and response system strengthened Indicator: All project-supported national and regional laboratories digitally provide real-time sex- and age-disaggregated test results to MOH for data analysis, decision-making, and data visualization (2020 baseline: 0) Achievement: N Progress/Status: Ongoing 75%. All ICT equipment for SES 145 SES laboratories (15 regional, 130 district) were delivered to end-users in January 2025. For enhanced LIS and EMID, contracts were signed with Uzinfocom in November 2024 for developing the software prototypes (minimum viable product-45% of work), which have now been completed. Additional contracts were signed with Uzinfocom in June 2025 to complete the remaining (55%) of work, which includes developing software and user-guides, and piloting (from July 2025) and roll-out in all 205 structural SES facilities of the SES (by October 2025). Data Source: MOH report, midterm review special audit, and post-project special audit reports, screenshots Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y Actual value: N
Resilience to outbreaks of COVID-19 and other public health emergencies reinforced

Treatment surge capacity for critical care increased to more than 3,500 functional intensive care units attended by trained medical staff Achievement: 4000 Progress/Status: Q3 2025: Achieved: by mid-2022, functional ICUs in mid-2022 was 4 000 beds (special infection hospitals located in Tashkent region (Zangiota) 2 separate blocks, each with 2000 beds) [functional ICUs in mid-2023 was 2 000 beds (special infection hospital located in Tashkent region (Zangiota), 1 separate block with 2000 bed was reserved for emergency response to COVID-19] [Note - WHO ended the PHEIC for COVID-19 on 5 May 2023]
Training of medical staff during COVID: Training (in-person and online) were organized for 16,894 employees of the project facilities in order to improve the skills to use the PPE and hazard prevention: from 17,962 female 14,908 (83%) were trained; from 2 684 male 1,986 (74%) were trained] Data Source: MOH report, PIU assessment of facilities, midterm review special audit, and post-project special audit reports

Testing surge capacity increased to 25,000 polymerase chain reaction (PCR) tests per day by trained lab technicians, with turnaround time of less than 24 hours for testing for COVID-19 Achievement: 28800 Progress/Status: Achieved Q3 2025: by mid-2022 there were a total of 172 PCR machines in the country, the daily test figure was 49 536 (turnaround of 12 hours) [In mid-2023 only 150 PCR machines were involved in testing COVID-19 and the daily test figure was 28 800 (turnaround of 8 hours)] [Note - WHO ended the PHEIC for COVID-19 on 5 May 2023] Data Source: Ministry of Health (MOH) report, Project Implementation Unit (PIU) assessment of facilities, midterm review special audit, and post-project special audit reports
